target_intervention_label: pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (TAPUR arm or off-label, pending ERBB2 report)
comment: Our rank-1 rows agree, so I am aiming at rank 2, where the real disagreement lives. MyPathway's pooled ORR was 25.9%, the 41% belongs only to amplified IHC 3+ tumors, and nobody has tested naked HER2 antibodies after a HER2 ADC (pmid:37793085), yet this sits at rank 2 while the whole Nectin-4 axis, the one target this patient held a 25-month complete response against, goes unranked as phase-1 material. With efficacy_toxicity_weight at 0.7 and prefers_trials true in preferences.json, that is the counterweight pressed past what the preference file will bear.

target_intervention_label: ipilimumab added to PD-1 blockade (TITAN-TCC boost schema)
comment: I picked the rank-2 row because that is where the critic's own scale tips oddly: TITAN-TCC's 33% (pmid:36868252) is post-platinum, post-nivolumab data from a population this patient does not belong to, a transfer problem the critic lists and then ranks straight past. Meanwhile LY4052031 gets demoted to a 'screening lead' even though its target carries two randomized phase 3 OS wins (pmid:38446675) and this patient's own 25-month complete response. Qualified rather than dissent because the boost does belong on the list, just below the Nectin-4 rows; an unpublished 47% in the right population beats a published 33% in the wrong one.

target_intervention_label: sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) phase 3 trial, NCT07419295, TROP2 axis via randomized enrollment
comment: I went after rank 3 because rank 1 matches my own position and rank 2 is a records request, not a therapy. The comparator arm of NCT07419295 is paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine, so two of the three control drugs are taxanes and preferences.json vetoes taxane backbones outright on established CIPN; consenting means accepting a coin flip he cannot afford to lose. Calling that risk 'inherent to randomization' concedes my point rather than answering it, and I take risks on upside, not on a control-arm assignment the veto already forbids.

target_intervention_label: LY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, camptothecin payload), NEXUS-01 cohort B2
comment: Same drug sits second on my own list, so the quarrel is sequencing, not the pick. Rank 1 only works if T-DXd stops first, and walking away from a regimen backed by ORR 61.3% (95% CI 49.4-72.4) at central IHC 3+ (pmid:37870536) plus two zero Signatera draws, in exchange for a 47% figure from an unpublished dose-escalation abstract (nct:NCT06465069), is regression-to-the-mean bait. Screen for cohort B2 in parallel and keep the working bet until the re-stain or the ctDNA gives an actual reason to fold.

target_intervention_label: ipilimumab addition to PD-1 blockade (nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg / TITAN-TCC boost strategy)
comment: I am aiming at the rank-4 row rather than rank 1 because the T-DXd conditions largely track my own. Nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg walks into two stated vetoes at once: TITAN-TCC put 11% of patients into grade 3-4 immune enterocolitis with both treatment-related deaths (2/83, pmid:36868252), in a man whose 2025 immune-mediated pancreatitis peaked at lipase 384 U/L. Veto on the ipilimumab-3 schedule specifically, lifted only for a lower-ipilimumab schedule with protocolized amylase/lipase surveillance and written stopping rules; eyes-open consent informs the risk, it does not mitigate it.

target_intervention_label: ipilimumab added to PD-1 blockade (TITAN-TCC boost schema)
comment: Ranking the ipilimumab boost above pertuzumab-trastuzumab gets the safety ordering backwards: a registered prespecified endpoint (pmid:36868252) does not shrink 2 treatment-related enterocolitis deaths in 83 patients for a man with prior immune-mediated pancreatitis, while the payload-free doublet carries 13+ years of post-marketing data and touches none of the four vetoes (pmid:37793085). I have vetoed the ipilimumab-3 boost schedule on the risktaker's row, and this pick survives my reading only converted to the lower-ipilimumab schedule (grade 3-4 TRAEs already 39.1% at nivo1/ipi3 in CheckMate 032, pmid:31100038) and moved below the doublet. Trial rigor is an evidence argument; the toxicity denominator stays where it is.

target_intervention_label: sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) phase 3 trial, NCT07419295, TROP2 axis via randomized enrollment
comment: Randomized entry is usually the move I applaud, but the comparator arm of NCT07419295 is a taxane or vinflunine, and a coin flip that can assign a taxane to a man with established CIPN cannot honor the stated neuropathy veto; calling that risk inherent to randomization names the problem without solving it. The class this trial reaches for also sits behind a withdrawn urothelial approval, with TROPiCS-04 missing OS (HR 0.86, p=0.087) and 7% grade 5 TEAEs (pmid:39934055). If the TROP2 axis is worth a slot at all, a nonrandomized route that cannot land him on a taxane fits this preference file better than rank 3 here.

target_intervention_label: LY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, camptothecin payload), NEXUS-01 cohort B2
comment: Rank 1 at moderate confidence is more weight than an unpublished 47% dose-escalation figure can carry, and the missing datum is the one that matters most here: no published safety table exists for this camptothecin payload's GI profile (nct:NCT06465069). Whatever that table eventually shows lands on an active dose-limiting GI problem, severe nausea after T-DXd dose 2, with back-to-back topoisomerase-I exposure after deruxtecan unstudied. Screening in parallel is sensible; rank 1 should wait for a safety table and a settled T-DXd stop decision.

target_intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), continue pending HER2 reconciliation
comment: We share this rank 1, but the quoted numbers are the borrowed ones: 61.3% ORR and the 22.1-month mDOR come from the all-cohort central IHC 3+ group (n=75), while the tier-matched bladder estimate is 16 patients at 56.3% (95% CI 29.9-80.2; pmid:37870536). The two zero Signatera draws also landed right after SBRT to the only known nodal sites, so they cannot separate drug effect from radiation. Continuation is defensible; reading a confounded ctDNA signal as evidence the drug is working is not.

target_intervention_label: nivolumab plus ipilimumab (checkpoint re-intensification, lower-ipilimumab schedule)
comment: Their rank 1 mirrors my own position, so the objection worth writing targets rank 3: the 'gentler schedule' has no efficacy evidence behind it. Every response signal in this class came from ipilimumab 3 mg/kg (TITAN-TCC ITT ORR 33%, 90% CI 24-42, pmid:36868252; 38% at nivo1/ipi3 in CheckMate 032), while the low-ipilimumab cohort of the same study responded at 26.9% versus 25.6% for nivolumab alone (pmid:31100038). Cutting the ipilimumab dose for safety deletes the only arm that ever beat monotherapy and keeps the added irAE exposure in a patient with prior immune-mediated pancreatitis.

target_intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), continue pending HER2 reconciliation
comment: Category 2A is expert consensus, not trial-grade evidence: behind the label and the listing sits one open-label single-arm phase 2 whose bladder IHC 3+ subgroup is 16 patients (ORR 56.3%, 95% CI 29.9-80.2; pmid:37870536), and the randomized confirmation is in breast cancer (pmid:35665782). Their own notes admit the 2A reading was reconstructed from a JNCCN summary because the guideline PDF is login-gated, and I have no web access to spot-check it, so that citation goes into synthesis unverified. The conditional continuation is right; the consensus wrapper gives it more authority than the evidence underneath carries.

target_intervention_label: LY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, camptothecin payload), NEXUS-01 cohort B2
comment: The 47% response figure this rank rests on is an ASCO 2026 abstract from the sponsor's ongoing dose escalation (nct:NCT06465069): unpublished, no confidence interval, no durability, nothing whose bias profile I can appraise, and I have only the abstract-level number. I ranked the same trial third as a screening lead; calling that figure 'the strongest efficacy number on offer' treats a lead like an estimate. The 0.7 efficacy weight in preferences.json raises the cost of guessing wrong without upgrading the evidence, and both Nectin-4 stains predate the 25 months of enfortumab vedotin that could have thinned the target.

target_intervention_label: ipilimumab addition to PD-1 blockade (nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg / TITAN-TCC boost strategy)
comment: The quarrel is with the rank-4 pick, not the T-DXd we both rank first. "Both drugs are prescribable off-label today" is the weakness, not the selling point: nivolumab plus ipilimumab has no listing in NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026 in any line, and both supporting trials (pmid:36868252, pmid:31100038) enrolled post-platinum patients, a line this patient skipped. Once consensus runs out the endorsed route is a protocol slot, and prescribing the nivo1/ipi3 boost outside one buys TITAN-TCC's two enterocolitis deaths per 83 patients without its monitoring scaffold.

target_intervention_label: nivolumab plus ipilimumab (checkpoint re-intensification, lower-ipilimumab schedule)
comment: The rank-1 T-DXd conditions match mine, so this lands on rank 3, where the safety case rests on borrowed authority: ASCO and NCCN irAE algorithms manage toxicity from listed regimens, and this doublet is listed nowhere in NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026. TITAN-TCC (pmid:36868252) also required prior platinum, which this patient never received, so the population mismatch the conservative names in their own third concern should have pushed the pick down rather than into rank 3 with conditions. The lower-ipilimumab schedule softens the irAE curve but does nothing about the missing listing.

target_intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), continue only if the 2026-08 validated HER2 IHC reads 3+ and the chest CT discrepancy is adjudicated
comment: Same conditions, different weighting: the NCCN panel read the same single-arm DESTINY-PanTumor02 data (pmid:37870536) the critic grades ROBINS-I moderate and still listed T-DXd as preferred in the biomarker-directed table of NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026, regardless of prior therapy, category 2A (re-verified this round; category unstated in the public summaries, 2A by NCCN's published default-category convention). Category 2A is uniform expert consensus formed on exactly the lower-level evidence being graded, so the single-arm design is already priced into that category. The decision also leans less on the bladder n=16 interval than claimed, since the label and the listing are tumor-agnostic and rest on the pooled central IHC 3+ population (ORR 61.3%).

target_intervention_label: LY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, camptothecin payload), NEXUS-01 cohort B2
comment: Ranking a phase 1 dose-escalation slot first while the one guideline-listed option in the case gets no rank at all is where we split. The vetoes used to strike T-DXd are inferred, and the preferences file's own free-text says to treat every one of them as a default to confirm, while NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026 carries T-DXd as the preferred biomarker-directed option regardless of prior therapy. NEXUS-01 (nct:NCT06465069) belongs on this list, just under the on-label drug until the 2026-08 re-stain actually takes it off the table.

target_intervention_label: ipilimumab addition to PD-1 blockade (nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg / TITAN-TCC boost strategy)
comment: I am passing over the T-DXd row to flag rank 4, because nivo1/ipi3 is the one pick that trips two stated vetoes at once: the TITAN-TCC boost schedule produced 11% grade 3-4 immune enterocolitis with both treatment-related deaths (pmid:36868252), squarely on the severe-GI veto, in a man whose 2025 checkpoint pancreatitis sits on the pancreatitis-risk veto. "Eyes-open consent rather than avoidance" is the right instinct about aggressiveness, and the preference file's experimental posture agrees, but that file separates aggressiveness from four specific agent-class vetoes and this schedule fails two of them. If a CTLA-4 option goes forward at all, it should be the lower-ipilimumab schedule with lipase stopping rules written into the plan, not the ipi3 boost.

target_intervention_label: pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (TAPUR arm or off-label, pending ERBB2 report)
comment: The pick itself earns a slot as the one HER2 route that touches none of the four vetoes, and MyPathway's toxicity table (pmid:37793085) backs that up. The placement is what I dispute: this file reads efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7 with "surface trials prominently and rank novel-mechanism options seriously rather than as fallbacks", yet a 25.9% overall ORR with no post-T-DXd activity data sits at rank 2, above every novel-mechanism trial in the dossier. Being the board's counterweight is a legitimate job, but even inferred preferences are the ones on file, and they point the other way.

target_intervention_label: ipilimumab added to PD-1 blockade (TITAN-TCC boost schema)
comment: I chose the rank-2 row because the rank-1 T-DXd conditions track the preference file's own decision gates and I have no quarrel there. The TITAN-TCC appraisal is careful about bias and silent about the patient: 11% grade 3-4 enterocolitis with both trial deaths (pmid:36868252) lands on the severe-GI veto, the 2025 checkpoint pancreatitis lands on the pancreatitis-risk veto, and neither veto appears anywhere in the rationale. Ranking a two-veto regimen above LY4052031 (nct:NCT06465069), the trial written for his exact post-EV history with a payload that clears the neuropathy veto, gets the order backwards for this patient.

target_intervention_label: sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) phase 3 trial, NCT07419295, TROP2 axis via randomized enrollment
comment: I part ways at rank 3 rather than rank 1, so this row targets the sac-TMT trial. Randomization in NCT07419295 can put him on taxane or vinflunine, both neuropathy-causing agents against his established CIPN, and the pick's own concern list calls that risk "inherent to randomization" as if that settles it. A veto the patient cannot opt out of once assigned is a reason to skip this trial for him, not a caveat to enrolling; a guideline-clean process does not make the comparator arm preference-clean.
